name: The Crown's Debt
about: The bankers across the sea want back what your father borrowed. Squeeze the houses, pay with what the crown has, or refuse and face the sellswords the bankers hire, and the lord they choose to back.
title: The Crown's Debt

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: A grey ship docks at the river mouth. A man in grey walks into Kingsmere with your father's seal on a note for more gold than the crown has ever had.

court.text: {rich} of {rich.house}, who knows the bankers well: "They want their gold, Your Grace, and they always get it, one way or another."

options.label: Pay the first part from the treasury (500 gold)
options.hint: The bankers wait, but the crown's coffers are empty
options.result: The crown pays. The man in grey bows and says he'll be back in a year for the next part.

options.label: Make the great houses pay a special tax
options.result: A special tax goes out under the King's seal. Every great house pays, and every great house remembers it.

options.label: Refuse: the crown doesn't pay its father's debts
options.hint: Nothing happens now, but the bankers have other ways
options.result: The King tears the note in half. The man in grey picks up both halves and goes to see {rich}.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: The man in grey comes back, just as he said. The second payment is bigger than the first.

court.text: {poor} of {poor.house}: "Another tax will ruin my house, Your Grace. Find another way, or I'll find another King who can."

options.label: Pay from the treasury again (600 gold)
options.hint: The debt is done, but the crown is poor
options.result: The crown pays the last of it. The man in grey sails home, and the treasury is empty.

options.label: Tax the houses again
options.result: The second tax goes out. {poor} pays it with silver plates from {poor.his} own table.

options.label: Refuse to pay the rest
options.hint: Nothing happens now, but the bankers turn to swords
options.result: The King refuses. The man in grey doesn't argue. He just leaves.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: The bankers' gold has bought a sellsword company, and the company has spent the winter at {bank} as {rich}'s guests.

court.text: {poor}: "Five thousand sellswords at {bank}, Your Grace, eating {rich}'s bread. Pay them off, or they'll come for what you owe with a different King."

options.label: Outbid the bankers for the sellswords (700 gold)
options.hint: The company changes sides, but you still owe the debt
options.result: The crown pays more than the bankers. The sellsword captain kneels to the King, for a year.

options.label: Take {bank} from {rich} for hiding them
options.result: By royal decree, {bank} goes to {poor.house}. {rich} doesn't open the gates.

beats.speaker: rich
beats.text: With the bankers' gold and the bankers' swords, {rich} says a crown that can't pay its debts can't keep its throne, and marches.

beats.speaker: poor
beats.text: The debt is paid, one way or another, and the grey ship doesn't come back. The houses count what it cost them.

beats.speaker: poor
beats.text: The bankers' man is beaten outside Kingsmere. The crown never pays, and never borrows across the sea again.
